title: Halcyon night watch — handoff sketch
content:
Quick TL;DR:
- Quiet night overall. Two small blips: token-service latency spike ~02:10 UTC, memcached eviction storm at ~04:05 UTC. Both self-healed after ~6–10 minutes.
- Still running with temporary memcached sizing until infra-ops finishes the autoscale policy (INFR-4123).
- No customer-facing incidents; small internal rate-limit errors reported by batch-delivery jobs.

What I saw (chronological):
- 01:50 UTC: routine health checks green.
- 02:08 UTC: Pager: token-service p50 p95 latency breach (p95 ~1.9s). Alert threshold 1.5s.
  - Quick check: token-service pod restarted once (k8s) at 02:06 UTC. Logs show GC pause spike and ephemeral OOM warning from sidecar telemetry.
  - Action taken: redeployed pod replica (kubectl rollout restart deploy/token-service) — latency returned to baseline by 02:16.
  - Note: need to correlate with node pressure metrics; node kubelet logs had brief docker-shim warnings.
- 04:03 UTC: memcached eviction rate spiked (cache miss ratio rose).
  - Cause: batch job lambda (delivery-bridge) replayed ~40k keys due to a mis-scheduled retry window.
  - Temporary mitigation: scaled memcached horizontally + bumped memory on primary instance (console -> infra -> memcache -> edit pool). Evictions returned to normal by 04:12.
  - Root cause: the batch-retry job's cron overlap bug (ticket: JOBS-982).

Open/Ongoing items for next shift:
- INFR-4123 (memcached autoscale): infra-ops is testing config changes in staging. Still waiting on final commit. If eviction spikes again, don't bother restarting memcached — instead scale pool + open a support ticket with cloud provider (internal runbook step 7).
- JOBS-982: delivery-bridge retry window fix scheduled for today's deploy. Watch for any high-volume replays.
- Token-service: still investigating GC patterns. Suspicion: the new telemetry sidecar spikes memory at cold-start. Add a pre-shutdown warmup window if we see more restarts.

Temporary runbook sketch (do this first for token-service latency alerts):
1) Check alert details: Grafana -> alert history. Confirm which container/pod.
2) kubectl -n token get pods -o wide | grep token-service
3) kubectl logs -n token <pod> -c token-main --since=15m | tail -n 200 
   - Look for GC, OOM, or repeated error messages referencing "kv-cache" or "telemetry"
4) kubectl describe pod <pod> to see recent events (oom, evicted, killed)
5) If restarted < 10 minutes ago and CPU < 80%: wait 5m and monitor, else: kubectl rollout restart deploy/token-service
6) If multiple pods failing or node pressure: cordon node, drain, and escalate to SRE lead (see contacts).

Temporary commands I ran (keep for context):
- kubectl -n token get pods -o wide | grep token-service
- kubectl logs -n token token-service-5b9f7 -c token-main --since=20m | egrep "GC|OOM|error"
- kubectl rollout restart deploy/token-service --namespace=token
- gcloud memcache instances update memcache-primary --size=2GB --project=redwood-prod (used console for scaling)

Escalation / contact list (short):
- Oncall SRE (primary): Maya Chen (me) — slack @maya, pager oncall rotation.
- SRE lead: Alex Torres — ping Slack and call if >30min unresolved.
- Infra-ops: Riley Patel — for autoscaling/memcache edits.
- Platform Eng Pager: +1 (555) 867-5309 (internal extension 8675309) — for node-wide issues.
- Customer escalation: cust-succ@redwood.com (only if customer impact confirmed).

Notes / heuristics I've been using (mental checklist):
- If p95 spikes but only one pod affected: pod-level flake — check restart history and sidecar logs.
- If p95 spikes across >=50% pods: likely infra or upstream (kafka, db). Check kafka consumer lag and db CPU.
- Memcached evictions: if >5% sustained for >5 minutes, scale or increase memory; avoid restarts during traffic peak — prefer adding nodes.

Questions for follow-up / TODOs I couldn't finish:
- Add a small warmup for telemetry sidecar to reduce cold-start memory jump (talk to @platform-telemetry).
- Write a short playbook snippet for batch job retry windows that infra/cust-eng can reference (owner: Riley).
- Validate whether token-service GC tuning set in staging matches prod. If mismatch, sync.

Small personal scratch notes (raw):
- Maybe add a short tag to alerts: "kv-cache" vs "telemetry" so oncall knows which mitigation applies.
- Think about adding a preflight check to the batch job that aborts if memcache eviction rate >2%.
- Peace-of-mind: keep an eye on delivery-bridge commit flagged in JOBS-982 after deploy window (12:30 UTC).

If you take over:
- Read the alert in Grafana first, then jump to pods -> logs. Try not to restart whole deployment unless multiple pods or clear node pressure.
- If unsure, message me on Slack @maya; I'll be around for the first 30m after handoff.

End of sketch. This is intentionally messy — please copy into a formal runbook when we have consensus.
